comparison: Both evaluate the experimental design and mouse model (C12-C19, C30-C31). OpenEval provides detailed methodological assessment including sequencing depth and sample sizes. Peer reviewers affirm the model's validity and utility without critique. Both find the approach SUPPORTED.

Both assess diversity analysis and comparable response magnitude between eCD4 and eTreg (C40-C42, C70-C71). OpenEval emphasizes statistical methods and normalization. Peer reviewers highlight the breadth of immune response findings. Both find evidence SUPPORTED, with peer review also including C20-C21 summary claims.

Both evaluate repertoire overlap showing distinct clustering of eCD4 and eTreg (C43, C72). OpenEval focuses on F2 metric methodology. Peer reviewers accept this as a core finding with C22 summary claim included. Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

Perfect alignment on convergent responses and challenge-specific motifs (C44-C45, C73-C74). OpenEval validates TCRNET clustering approach. Peer reviewers describe evidence as 'solid' and affirm convergent motif identification. Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate cancer challenge repertoire similarity suggesting shared tumor antigens (C46, C75). OpenEval notes alternative explanations not ruled out but finds interpretation reasonable. Peer reviewers accept the tumor-specific clustering as 'convincing.' Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

Both assess tissue-specific localization of antigen-focused responses (C49-C53, C76). OpenEval emphasizes MDS analysis and appropriate controls. Peer reviewers affirm challenge-specific and tissue-specific responses. Both find evidence SUPPORTED, with peer review also including background claim C48.

Both evaluate cross-tissue antigen-driven similarity (C54-C55, C81). OpenEval highlights comparable convergence between eCD4 and eTreg. Peer reviewers accept this as part of antigen-specificity demonstration with 'solid' evidence. Both find evidence SUPPORTED, though peer review includes fewer specific claims (C56-C57 not included).

Perfect alignment on tumor-specific clonal conversion evidence (C23-C24, C47, C58-C61, C77-C78). OpenEval emphasizes nucleotide-level stringency and local nature. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge 'occasional plasticity' with 'convincing evidence.' Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate iNKT conversion in LLC tumors (C25-C26, C63-C65, C79). OpenEval highlights tumor-specificity versus other challenges. Peer reviewers accept as part of plasticity findings with 'convincing evidence.' Both find evidence SUPPORTED, with peer review also including background claim C62.

Both assess mechanistic interpretation of tumor-induced plasticity (C27). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting mechanism not directly tested and alternative explanations not ruled out. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the interpretation as part of overall 'solid' and 'convincing' findings. This represents a key disagreement in evaluation stringency.

Perfect alignment on tissue-resident, antigen-specific Treg populations (C28-C29, C66-C68, C82-C83). OpenEval emphasizes novel finding and appropriate exclusion of challenge site. Peer reviewers affirm tissue-specific responses with 'solid' evidence. Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate stronger tissue-specific convergence in eTreg versus eCD4 (C69). OpenEval focuses specifically on this comparative finding. Peer reviewers include broader comparative analysis (C56-C57, C84-C85) emphasizing antigen-specific Treg nature. Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

OpenEval assesses comparative findings between eCD4 and eTreg (C84-C85) as SUPPORTED. Peer R12 includes these claims along with C56-C57, C69 in broader comparative analysis, also finding evidence SUPPORTED. Substantial overlap in assessed comparative conclusions.

OpenEval evaluates main findings summary (C20-C22, C86) as SUPPORTED. Peer R13 assesses model utility and conclusions (C86-C87) as SUPPORTED with strong affirmation from all reviewers. Both validate overall conclusions, though OpenEval notes developmental origins not directly tested.

OpenEval assesses model's demonstration of convergent responses (C87) as SUPPORTED. Peer R13 includes C87 with C86 in overall validation of model utility and conclusions. Both strongly affirm the model's value and successful demonstration.

Both evaluate experimental methods (C88-C106). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of sample sizes, CD45 labeling, and standard approaches. Peer reviewers accept methods without critique, noting 'well accepted tools' and improved clarity. Both find methods SUPPORTED, with peer review also including sequencing claims C32-C37.

Perfect alignment on computational methods (C107-C126). OpenEval validates UMI quantification, normalization, diversity metrics, and quality control as best practices. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'state of the art analyses using well accepted tools.' Both find methods SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate background/contextual claims (C1-C11, C38-C39). OpenEval notes these are well-supported by citations and require no primary data evaluation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through overall positive assessment. Both find background claims SUPPORTED, with some differences in claim coverage (OpenEval includes C48, C62, C80).
